title: Native run
description: One run of one application over a list of OPF-exported .pptx files: the run.json at the top of a native run directory. Each file's own result is files/<fileId>/result.json (native-result.schema.json). scripts/native-acceptance/core/result/README.md explains it.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this format. Always 1.

target.description: The application under test: "keynote" (Keynote on macOS), "powerpoint" (PowerPoint on Windows), "impress" (LibreOffice Impress), "powerpoint-mac" (PowerPoint on macOS).

application.description: The application as it reports itself. Read from the application at run time, never hard-coded.

build.description: Its build number when known (for example "7052.0.68").

system.description: The operating system the application ran on.

fonts.description: Which fonts the application could use: "installed" (whatever the machine has), or a named font profile (Impress: "opf", "stock").

opf.description: The OPF that exported the input.

commit.description: The git commit it was built from, when it was not a published release.

tier.description: Which set of decks the run covered: "smoke" (about ten decks), "release" (the qualification corpus), "full" (corpus, examples, gallery layouts, language decks); null for a hand-picked list.

baseline.description: The OPF version whose results this run is compared with (for example "0.36.0"); null for none.

check.description: What the driver's check verb said before the run.

status.description: "ready": the machine could run the target. "refused": it could not, and no file was opened.

reasons.description: Why it refused (for example "the screen is locked"), or notes when ready; empty when there is nothing to say.

files.description: One entry per input file, in run order.

deck.description: The deck the file was exported from.

variant.description: Which export of the deck ("default" when there is one).

result.description: The file's result, relative to the run directory: files/<id>/result.json.

open.description: The status of the file's open verb, repeated here so a reader of run.json sees failures at once.

slideCount.description: How many slides the opened file has, hidden slides counted; null when it did not open.
